property_summary: Only the contract owner can withdraw the contract balance (withdrawAll) — calls by non-owners must not transfer Ether out.
Calls to withdrawAll revert for callers that are not the contract owner (i.e., non-owners cannot successfully call withdrawAll).

For any payable caller, withdrawAll always routes the current contract balance through the internal withdraw(uint) function (so an overriding/guarded withdraw can prevent funds leaving); the mutant bypasses withdraw(uint) and thus will transfer out balance even when a malicious/guarding override would block/rewind, so there exist inputs (a re-entrancy/guarding adversary) where reference preserves balance while mutant does not.

For any caller and any deposit amount, when withdrawAll is invoked by the owner, the correct contract routes the payout through withdraw(uint) so a malicious/guarding override in a callee (which rejects receiving Ether) can prevent funds leaving the contract (leaving address(c).balance unchanged), whereas the mutant directly transfers the balance and will succeed in sending Ether to the callee (changing address(c).balance); thus the reference always preserves balance==0 after a failing external recipient causes withdraw to revert, while the mutant may not.

For any recipient contract that reverts on plain transfer, the reference C routes withdrawals through withdraw(uint) (which can be overridden to block or revert), so after withdrawAll the contract balance remains unchanged for all such adversarial recipients and inputs; the mutant that uses payable(msg.sender).transfer(address(this).balance) instead will attempt a direct transfer and thus can change address(c).balance for some inputs, breaking the rule.

For any caller and any payable deposit, when withdrawAll is invoked by the owner the reference contract routes the payout through withdraw(uint) so a malicious recipient that reverts on receiving Ether (or blocks via an overridden withdraw) causes withdrawAll to leave the contract balance unchanged; the mutant that does a direct transfer can change the contract balance for some inputs (the adversarial recipient), violating this rule.

For any recipient contract that reverts when receiving Ether (causing a low-level call from withdraw to fail), calling withdrawAll as owner on the reference C always leaves address(c).balance unchanged (withdraw routed through withdraw which fails), whereas the mutant that directly does payable(msg.sender).transfer(address(this).balance) can change address(c).balance for some recipient (the transfer will attempt and may succeed or behave differently), so the mutant can reduce the contract balance while the reference cannot.

Reference: only the owner can cause the contract to transfer its full balance via withdrawAll, so after any caller invokes withdrawAll the contract balance is zero only when called by the owner; Mutant: removing the onlyOwner guard allows non-owners to withdraw the full balance — thus there exist callers and balances where a non-owner call makes address(c).balance == 0 but in the reference the same non-owner call would not (owner-only restriction prevents it).

For every caller and Ether balance, only the owner can successfully make the contract transfer out its entire balance via withdrawAll; removing onlyOwner allows some non-owner caller to drain the contract (address(c).balance == 0) while in the reference that same non-owner call would leave balance > 0.

For every caller address and contract balance, calling withdrawAll as a non-owner must revert (or be disallowed) so that non-owners cannot change the contract balance to zero; the mutant removing onlyOwner allows some non-owner to successfully drain the contract, violating this property.

In the reference, only the owner can cause the contract to forward ETH out via withdrawAll, therefore when ANY non-owner calls withdrawAll the contract's balance must remain unchanged (still equal to its prior balance); the mutant removing onlyOwner allows some non-owner call to reduce address(c).balance (sometimes to zero) — the test fuzzes caller and amount and shows a non-owner can change c's balance on the mutant but not on the reference.

For all callers and deposit amounts, in the correct contract only the owner can cause withdrawAll to succeed (so a non-owner's attempt to call withdrawAll must revert), whereas the mutant removes the onlyOwner guard allowing some non-owners to successfully call withdrawAll; the test fuzzes caller and deposit amount and asserts that a non-owner's withdrawAll call always reverts (the correct contract) — a property the mutant violates for some inputs.

For any nonzero deposit amount sent to the contract by any account, calling withdrawAll by the owner will reduce the contract balance (reference: withdraws full balance); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave the balance unchanged for some deposits and thus violates this rule.

For any positive deposit made to C, calling withdrawAll by the owner drains the contract balance to zero (reference); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave a positive balance, violating this rule for some deposits.

If the owner calls withdrawAll after ANY positive balance has been sent into the contract, the call succeeds (does not revert) and reduces the contract balance by at least 1 wei; the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave the balance unchanged causing this property to fail for some fuzzed deposit amounts and depositors.

For any owner and any prior nonzero deposit amount sent into C, calling withdrawAll by the owner makes the contract balance strictly less than it was before the call; the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave the balance unchanged and thus violates this rule for some inputs.

For any fuzzed nonzero deposit amount sent into C by any depositor, when the owner calls withdrawAll the contract's balance becomes strictly less than before (reference drains balance; mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave balance unchanged).

For any caller who is the owner and for any contract balance >= 1, calling withdrawAll always reduces the contract balance to zero (reference); the mutant that calls withdraw(1) leaves a nonzero contract balance for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller who is the owner and any positive contract balance, calling withdrawAll drains the contract balance to zero; the mutant that withdraws a fixed 1 wei can leave a nonzero contract balance for some positive balances.

For any owner caller and any contract balance B >= 0, after owner calls withdrawAll the contract's balance equals max(0, B - B) = 0 (i.e., withdrawAll drains the contract); the mutant that calls withdraw(1) can leave a nonzero contract balance when B > 1, violating this rule.

For any owner caller and any contract balance >= 0, calling withdrawAll drains the contract balance to zero; the mutant that calls withdraw(1) can leave a nonzero contract balance when the balance > 1.

For any owner caller and any contract balance B, after the owner calls withdrawAll the contract's balance decreases by exactly B (i.e., becomes zero); the mutant that always withdraws 1 wei instead only decreases balance by 1 for B>0, violating this rule for many inputs.
After increasing the contract balance via fallback deposits, owner can always withdraw up to the contract balance (withdraw does not revert) for any value ≤ prior deposits total.
Calling withdraw never reverts (for any _value) on the original contract, so the test asserts withdraw does not revert.
On the original contract, calling withdraw(x) by the owner never reverts even when x exceeds the contract balance, so if the caller is the owner then withdrawn call does not revert.
If the caller is the contract owner, then calling withdraw(...) never reverts on the original contract, so reverted must be false when msg.sender is owner.
If the caller is NOT the contract owner, calling withdraw(...) will revert (only owner can call withdraw on the original), so reverted must be true for non-owners.

For any target address and amount, calling sendMoney(target, amount) forwards the call and does not change the contract's ability to later withdraw the same amount (i.e., owner can always withdraw up to address(this).balance afterwards); the mutant that pre-checks balance before transfer can cause withdraw to fail when sendMoney sent funds externally such that the contract balance decreased (e.g., target reverts or consumes funds), breaking this invariant for some inputs.

For any target and value, if sendMoney(target, value) returns normally then the contract's balance decreases by exactly value (so the owner can later withdraw that value); the mutant that adds require(address(this).balance >= _value) in withdraw can make a later withdraw fail for some sequences where sendMoney forwarded funds out and reduced balance, violating the invariant that a successful sendMoney of value permits the owner to withdraw that same value afterwards.

For any target contract that may revert on receiving funds, if sendMoney(target, value) returns normally then the owner can still withdraw value from C later; the mutant that pre-checks balance in withdraw can be broken when sendMoney forwards funds out (or causes balance changes) such that withdraw's precondition fails while the original transfer semantics still allowed the prior successful sendMoney to complete.

For any target address and amount that sendMoney(target, amount) CALLS and returns successfully, the contract's balance never decreases below 0 and the owner can withdraw up to address(c).balance afterwards (i.e., after a successful sendMoney call that returned normally, calling withdraw(address(this).balance) should succeed on the reference but can fail on the mutant that requires balance>=_value), so the property asserts that a successful sendMoney does not prevent withdrawing the contract's current balance.

For any amount X and any recipient helper that may consume funds, if the owner successfully calls sendMoney(helper, X) (the call returns normally), then the contract's balance decreases by at most X and the owner can still withdraw the contract's entire current balance; the mutant that adds a precondition require(address(this).balance >= _value) inside withdraw can make withdraw revert for some sequences where sendMoney consumed funds and left balance lower than a previously-expected withdrawal amount.
Only the owner can make the contract send out ether via withdraw; non-owners cannot reduce the contract balance by calling withdraw.
